principles: Local-first then authority: every authority POST is gated behind passing local validation; a command never sends a POST it cannot locally justify (Blockers 1+2).

Zero divergence by construction: in enforce mode the authority POST happens BEFORE the local evidence commit (pre-POST verification), so an authority failure leaves no local write at all — not even transiently (Blocker 4, user-chosen 2026-05-21).

Mode-graded blast radius: off = byte-identical to post-B-2157 main (default when env unset/invalid); shadow = authority is observational only (warning-only, never mutates local state, Blocker 3); enforce = authority is gating.

Additive, non-regressive extension: submission protocol is added as NEW exports beside B-2157's VCP exports; VCP digest / normalization / pack behavior stays byte-identical, guarded by test:verification-context-pack-smoke + test:process-fact-contract as hard blockers.

No new command surface: authority submission is a behavior of the existing verification_evidence_add / batch_add (via authorityMode / authorityURL args + KOALA_AUTHORITY_MODE / KOALA_AUTHORITY_URL env), not a new koala command — keeps ownership / process-fact registries unchanged.
drivers: The cross-repo Python authority server enforces an anti-hallucination evidence gate; the CLI must submit structured evidence with a consistent protocol (verification-context-pack.md is the shared truth source).

2026-05-20 user probe found stash@{3} POSTs authority BEFORE local validation -> a non-existent itemId already produced 1 POST while local failed. Shipping that would create exactly the local/remote fact divergence the system exists to prevent.
B-2157 already shipped the VCP envelope structures (EvidenceEnvelopeContract, digests, normalization) on main; Story 2 must reuse, not duplicate or mutate them.
Incremental adoption: off/shadow/enforce lets the authority gate roll out without breaking the large existing population of off-mode verification_evidence_add callers.

options.name: A-prepost
pros: Zero divergence window: authority POST before local commit means authority failure -> no local write ever, not even transient.
batch_add is naturally all-or-nothing: one batch POST gates the whole local write set.
No rollback exit-safety needed (no kill-9 mid-rollback divergence window).
Simplest invariant for the reviewer to verify mechanically.
cons: enforce mode cannot write evidence offline: if the authority server is down, local evidence write also fails (this is the intended semantics of enforce, not a defect).

options.name: B-rollback
pros: Local evidence could be written first (closer to shadow-mode code path).
cons: Two-phase commit: a kill-9 between local write and rollback leaves PERMANENT local-has / authority-doesn't divergence.
batch rollback must atomically remove N entries; rollback failing on entry K leaves K-1 stale entries needing recovery.
Rollback logic itself needs a smoke proving it never partially fails — extra surface for the exact bug class we are preventing.

options.name: C-separate-command
pros: Authority submission isolated in its own koala command, evidence handlers untouched.
cons: Splits the evidence flow: a user could write local evidence and never submit, breaking enforce-mode coupling.
Adds command surface -> new command-policy ownershipClass + PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY entries + gate wiring.
stash@{3} did NOT take this path (authority is integrated into evidence handlers via params) — diverging would discard the reference implementation's shape.

rationale: Pre-POST verification is the only option with a zero divergence window: authority failure short-circuits before any local write, so local and authority states can never disagree even under kill-9. It makes batch_add all-or-nothing for free and needs no rollback exit-safety. B-rollback reintroduces the two-phase-commit divergence window this story exists to eliminate; C-separate-command breaks the enforce-mode coupling between local evidence and authority and adds command surface. Additive-only extension + hard-blocker VCP smokes protect B-2157's shipped behavior; env-var + arg config and no-new-command keep the registries untouched. User chose option (a) on 2026-05-21.

preMortem.scenario: An additive edit to authority-contracts.ts accidentally changes a helper shared by both VCP and submission (e.g. canonicalJson / digestCanonical body or signature).
preMortem.trigger: Implementer refactors an existing export instead of adding a new one, or 'tidies' a shared function while adding submission types.
preMortem.consequence: VCP digest output changes -> B-2157 pack behavior breaks -> test:verification-context-pack-smoke fails; downstream verifier digests mismatch the Python server.
preMortem.mitigation: test:verification-context-pack-smoke + test:process-fact-contract are hard blockers (block REVIEW->TEST). Reviewer diff-checks that every existing export body is byte-identical and only NEW exports were added. CHK-001 forbids touching the protected names.

preMortem.scenario: In shadow mode the authority client throws a non-HTTP exception (TypeError / DNS failure / parse error) that escapes the warning-only path.
preMortem.trigger: Unhandled exception branch in authority-client not wrapped by the shadow degradation catch.
preMortem.consequence: Command crashes / exits non-zero / skips the local evidence write -> Blocker 3 violated, shadow mode mutates or blocks local state.
preMortem.mitigation: Shadow-mode authority interaction wrapped in a catch-all that degrades ANY failure (HTTP error, timeout, throw, connection refused) to a single stderr [warning]; local write happens regardless. Smoke injects throw / timeout / 5xx / connection-refused under shadow and asserts exit 0 + local write + stderr warning.

preMortem.scenario: enforce-mode batch_add: the authority server accepts a PARTIAL batch (some entries ok, some rejected) and returns per-entry status.
preMortem.trigger: Authority API supports partial acceptance; client commits locally only the 'ok' subset.
preMortem.consequence: Local writes the accepted entries while the user's command reports failure -> partial local/remote agreement that is hard to reason about; violates all-or-nothing.
preMortem.mitigation: Treat the batch POST as atomic: local commit happens only if the authority accepts the WHOLE batch. If the authority returns any per-entry rejection, map it to a whole-batch failure (zero local writes) and surface which entries were rejected in the error. Smoke covers partial-rejection -> 0 local writes.

preMortem.scenario: KOALA_AUTHORITY_MODE unset or set to an invalid value is interpreted as enforce (or shadow) instead of off.
preMortem.trigger: Mode-parse fallback defaults to a non-off value, or empty string slips past the parser.
preMortem.consequence: Every existing verification_evidence_add caller suddenly needs a reachable authority server -> mass breakage of the off-mode population; the opposite of incremental rollout.
preMortem.mitigation: authority-mode.ts defaults to 'off' whenever the env var is unset / empty / whitespace / not one of off|shadow|enforce, with runtime re-validation per CLAUDE.md Handler 编码约定 (not Zod-only). An off-mode smoke asserts zero network traffic + byte-identical behavior to pre-Story-2 main.
